issues.description: The PTE physical-address mask retains bits 52 through 62, so reserved or software bits above the x86-64 physical-address field are returned as address bits.
issues.rationale: The problem mask 0x7fff_ffff_ffff_f000 covers bits 12-62, while the maximum-width x86-64 PTE physical-address field occupies bits 12-51. PageTableEntry(1usize << 52).paddr() therefore returns 1 << 52 instead of zero. Repair 20ba976d narrows the mask to 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000 (bits 12-51) and consistently applies it to construction, extraction, property masking, and proofs.
issues.source_evidence:
after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/pte/page_table_entry.rs:21-25
PHYS_ADDR_MASK is declared as 0x7fff_ffff_ffff_f000, retaining bit 52 and all bits through 62.

after/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/pte/page_table_entry.rs:374-382
paddr_spec and paddr both return self.0 & PHYS_ADDR_MASK(), so any retained high bit is exposed as address data.

repair/lock-protocol/src/exec/rw/pte/page_table_entry.rs:30-37 @ 20ba976dc4dc0943c3eda62b0d96cb8a37e41320
PHYS_ADDR_MASK becomes 0xF_FFFF_FFFF_F000, equivalent to 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000 and covering only bits 12-51.
issues.verification: Direct fixed-width witness: (1 << 52) & 0x7fff_ffff_ffff_f000 = 1 << 52, while (1 << 52) & 0x000f_ffff_ffff_f000 = 0. With Verus 0b6f3cbb/Rust 1.88/Z3 4.12.5, vstd_extra verifies 228/0 at both sides, problem lock-protocol verifies 501/0, and repaired/final verifies 497/0. Passing both is expected because x86 field width is an architectural source requirement, not a built-in verifier rule; the verifier revision postdates the PR.
